grep for 'abyssal|unmake|curse|support_damage|mandate' returns zero hits — the document contains no formula governing this leaf; its §2.1/§2.2 cover only m(R)=100/(100+R) and penetration order. The governing text is therefore the cached wiki effect text above.

independent_computation.rule_derived_from_the_wiki_text: Unmake is a proximity aura, not an unconditional owner-side amplifier. Reading the branch text literally, the amplification factor applied to a single damage packet P is: amp(P) = 1.12 if and only if ALL THREE gates hold — (g1) the victim is an enemy CHAMPION (the curse is only applied to 'Enemy champions'), (g2) the victim is within 700 units of the Abyssal Mask holder ('within 700 units of you', center-to-edge), and (g3) the packet's damage type is MAGIC ('receive 12% increased magic damage'). Otherwise amp(P) = 1 (i.e. no support multiplier authored). The clause 'from all sources' widens only the DEALER dimension (any ally, including the holder), it does not widen the DAMAGE TYPE dimension — the noun it modifies is 'magic damage'.
independent_computation.magnitude_check: 12% is the current cached value in both the wiki branch and Riot's own description, and data/staleness.json entry "8020" reports stale=false with zero stat_drift, so 1 + 0.12 = 1.12 is the correct magnitude WHEN the gates hold. The disputed leaf is therefore not a magnitude question but an applicability question.
independent_computation.composition_check: If both roster amplifiers were live on the same packet the receipt would have to read 1.12 × 1.07 = 1.1984 (Mandate's Command is explicitly 'from all sources' with no damage-type gate, so it is the WIDER of the two). The old leaf carried a bare 1.12 with a single source string, i.e. Mandate's Vulnerable mark was demonstrably NOT active on event 14 in the old baseline either. Consequently 'absent' on the new side is self-consistent: with Mandate's 4 s Vulnerable window not covering this event and Bloodletter's Curse contributing resistance reduction rather than a multiplier, the ONLY candidate multiplier at event 14 is Abyssal's 1.12, and dropping it must leave the key absent rather than falling back to 1.07 or 1.0.
independent_computation.evaluation_of_the_two_candidate_values: Old (1.12) is correct only if event 14 is a MAGIC packet dealt to an enemy champion inside the 700-unit aura. New (absent) is correct if event 14 fails any one of g1/g3 — a physical or true-damage packet (basic attacks and physical/true ability components are the common case in a mixed combat timeline of 15+ events), or a packet resolved against a non-champion target. The change is scoped to individual events inside a scenario that still equips the item (the scenario is named for it), which is the signature of a per-packet gate being enforced, not of the aura being deleted: a deletion would zero the multiplier on every event uniformly, including the magic ones.
independent_computation.conclusion: Under the quoted text there is NO reading in which Unmake amplifies a non-magic packet — every historical and current phrasing of this aura ('12% more magic damage', atom id 'damage.magic') restricts it to the magic type. A blanket 1.12 stamped on an event that the gates exclude is an over-application, and the wiki-faithful receipt for such an event is no support multiplier at all. The new value is therefore the one consistent with the cached source text.

residual_uncertainty.statement: The scenario definition and the golden baseline live under scripts/ and tests/, which this runbook forbids me to open, so I could not read which damage type or target event 14 carries. My verdict is the conditional resolved by the only text I am allowed to use.
residual_uncertainty.falsifier: If event 14 can be shown to be a MAGIC-damage packet dealt to an enemy champion within 700 units of the Abyssal Mask holder, then this verdict flips to old_value_correct and the new absence is a regression. Anyone with access to the scenario should check event 14's damage_type field before accepting this receipt.
residual_uncertainty.confidence: high on the rule (the wiki text is explicit and single-valued), moderate on the leaf verdict (depends on event 14's damage type, which I could not observe).
